title: Smart Contract Structure (PoDMPaymentProtocol)
purpose: Structure of the PoDMPaymentProtocol Solidity smart contract showing state variables, external payment functions, admin functions, events, and the PaymentType enum with their relationships
audience: Developers, smart contract auditors, blockchain engineers
description: The PoDMPaymentProtocol contract (147 lines, Solidity ^0.8.20) is an ERC-20 transferFrom-based payment splitter deployed on Base network. It has three state variables (owner, platformTreasury, platformFeeBps), three payment functions (paySubscription, payTip, payPPV) that split payments between platform treasury and creator via transferFrom, two admin functions (updateTreasury, updateFee) restricted by onlyOwner modifier with fee cap at 30%, and five events (SubscriptionPaid, TipPaid, PPVPaid, TreasuryUpdated, FeeUpdated). The PaymentType enum (Subscription, Tip, PPV) is used in events but NOT stored on-chain per payment. Key observations: no on-chain PaymentType storage, no SubscriptionExpired or SubscriptionCancelled events, no pause mechanism for emergency stops, and the contract is immutable with no upgrade mechanism.

decisions.truePath: Proceed with fee calculation and transfers

errorPaths.trigger: Fan has not approved enough USDC
errorPaths.recovery: Fan must call USDC.approve() with sufficient amount first
Only owner address can call admin functions

businessRules.rule: Only owner can update treasury or fee
Fee is capped at 30% (3000 basis points)
No on-chain storage of PaymentType per transaction — enum used only in events

securityConsiderations: No reentrancy vulnerability — transferFrom calls follow checks-effects-interactions pattern
Solidity 0.8+ provides built-in integer overflow protection
No selfdestruct or delegatecall — contract is permanent on-chain
No emergency pause mechanism — if vulnerability found, contract cannot be stopped
No upgradeability (no proxy pattern) — contract logic is immutable after deployment
Private key for owner address must be secured — it controls treasury and fee settings
tierIdHash and contentIdHash are bytes32 hashes — privacy measure but collisions theoretically possible
performanceConsiderations: Single transferFrom calls per split (2 total per payment) — gas efficient
No loops, no dynamic arrays — fixed gas cost per payment
Admin functions are rarely called — negligible gas impact

annotations.text: Contract uses ERC-20 transferFrom to pull USDC from sender (fan must approve first)
PaymentType enum exists in events but is NOT stored on-chain per payment — off-chain must parse event type from event signature
No SubscriptionExpired or SubscriptionCancelled events — subscriptions are one-time payments
No pause mechanism for emergency stops — if vulnerability found, contract cannot be halted
Contract is immutable — no proxy/upgrade mechanism. Any bug requires new deployment.
